newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow police arrest Vietnamese wanted in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Moscow police arrest Vietnamese wanted in Germany.

text.p: Russian police have arrested eight Vietnamese, including one wanted in Germany in connection with the slaying of seven of his compatriots last May, Itar-Tass news agency said on Tuesday.

Tass identified the man sought in Germany as Fan van Tien and said he was wanted for allegedly taking part in the cold-blooded execution of at least seven Vietnamese in Berlin during battles by rival gangs for a share of the black market.
German police found seven dead bodies, all of them tied up and shot in the head. All were known to have traded illegally in cigarettes.

The eight Vietnamese arrested in Moscow had entered Russia illegally, Tass said, adding that Tiehn would be extradited to Germany for investigation. There was no immediate confirmation of the Tass report from the police.

Many Vietnamese were brought to communist East Germany before 1989 as guest-workers and most have been seeking asylum there since the communist regime collapsed. As many as 63 Vietnamese have been killed in eastern Germany since 1992.
Thousands of former guest-workers from Vietnam are illegally staying in Russia, many of them also involved in black-market trade.
